paragraphs: Here's what I think Jesus wants you to walk away with, friend: prayer is talking to a Father. When the disciple asks, "Lord, teach us to pray," Jesus doesn't hand over a speech for impressing God. He starts with "Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come." (Luke 11:1-2). You come to God first, and then you bring Him your bread, your sins and your temptations, because He cares about the whole table.

Now the midnight story. The man at the door gets his bread, and Jesus says it's "because of the man's persistence" (Luke 11:8). Don't hear a grumpy neighbor in that. Hear Jesus saying, "Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you." (Luke 11:9). I think Jesus is inviting you to keep coming, friend, and I'd say that's the opposite of a closed door!

Then Jesus brings it home with a father and his kid. "If you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!" (Luke 11:13). Your Father is better than the best dad you can picture, so you don't have to be shy about asking. Keep asking, friend, and keep those ovens ready.
